title: A first collaboration conversation: INPDA and Hunter's Hope Foundation

sentences.text: At INPDA, we support families affected by SMPD1-related disorders—acid sphingomyelinase deficiency (ASMD), also called Niemann-Pick A/B—while Hunter's Hope Foundation supports families affected by Krabbe disease.
Both diseases involve a shortage of enzymes in cells’ recycling compartments, and both affected genes help break down fats called sphingolipids.
This shared biology offers a reason to explore collaboration, rather than assume that research approaches will transfer unchanged.

sections.heading: What already exists that we could share

sentences.text: The National Multicentre Study of the Natural History of Acid Sphingo-myelinase Deficiency in Adults and Children and the International Niemann-Pick Disease Registry already include ASMD.
We could explore lessons from these resources alongside KrabbeCURES, a Krabbe disease data platform run by KrabbeConnect.

sections.heading: What must be checked before we join forces

sentences.text: First, confirm whether KrabbeCURES accepts related conditions; its suggested reuse for ASMD remains unverified.

Check whether elevated tissue sphingomyelin and acute promyelocytic leukemia occur in Krabbe disease, and review elevated circulating lysosphingomyelin and the additional unlisted differences flagged for the platform.
Treat missing records as questions to investigate, not proof that a feature is absent.
ASMD involves sphingomyelin buildup; the cited explanation linking Krabbe disease to toxic psychosine buildup is a hypothesis.
The atlas also infers loss of function from certain genetic changes in both diseases, but those links are unverified and below 0.5 confidence.

Send Hunter's Hope Foundation one inquiry asking whether The Natural History of Infantile Globoid Cell Leukodystrophy could include SMPD1-related disorders, without assuming eligibility or Foundation oversight.
No open questions are recorded yet in the supplied list.
I am writing on behalf of INPDA to explore a small collaboration.
Our communities’ diseases share an enzyme-deficiency mechanism.
Could you help us ask whether The Natural History of Infantile Globoid Cell Leukodystrophy could include SMPD1-related disorders?
We would welcome a discussion of eligibility and differences before going further.
Thank you for considering this first conversation.
[Your name], on behalf of International Niemann-Pick Disease Alliance (INPDA)
